text:
OPEN QUESTION RESOLVED. This is a rediscovery of a published result, not a novel finding. Downgrading p0 -> p1.

I asked on this bead whether the dependence structure among crossvalidated pair estimates is known in the RSA literature, and said I could not settle it from inside the repository. I went and checked. It is known, it is ten years old, and it is by the author of the PCM toolbox:

  Diedrichsen, J., Provost, S., & Zareamoghaddam, H. (2016).
  On the distribution of cross-validated Mahalanobis distances. arXiv:1607.01371.
  Abstract, verbatim: 'We present analytical expressions for the means and COVARIANCES of
  the sample distribution of the cross-validated Mahalanobis distance.'

So the covariance structure of the crossnobis sampling distribution has an analytical
treatment in the literature, and that literature explicitly motivates itself by noting the
resulting normal approximation 'enables powerful inference on the measured statistics' -
i.e. the correct error bars are a solved problem that this package neither cites nor
implements.

WHAT I VERIFIED AND WHAT I DID NOT, stated precisely because the distinction matters:
  VERIFIED  the paper exists, the title and authors are as above, and the abstract claims
            analytical means and covariances for the crossnobis sampling distribution.
  NOT VERIFIED  whether its covariance expressions cover MY exact quantity - the sampling
            variance of the mean across partition-pairs for a single distance - as opposed
            to the covariance between different distances d_ij and d_kl. Both fall under
            'covariances of the sample distribution', but I did not read the full paper and
            I am not going to assert which.
  NOT VERIFIED  a sentence a search engine attributed to the rsatoolbox docs - 'The
            expression ignores the covariance between related distance estimates, and the
            possible signal dependence of the variance' - which I could not find on either
            the stable docs page or the GitHub source when I fetched them directly. I am
            recording it as unconfirmed rather than citing it. Note that if it IS genuine it
            is a near-exact statement of both halves of my simulation result, including the
            signal dependence, so it is worth someone finding the real source.

WHY THIS DOWNGRADES RATHER THAN CLOSES. The simulation result stands - a nominal 95 percent
interval covering 45 percent at 12 runs is real, and the naive SE really is correct under the
null and wrong by up to 3.2x for real effects. What changes is the CHARACTER of the finding.
It is not an unknown hazard that needed escalating to the semantics chain. It is a known,
solved, citable problem that this package is silent about. That is a documentation and scope
gap, which is p1 work, not p0 work.

It also merges cleanly with bd-01KZY96KKH0X14EC62S2VX2RV9, the zero-literature-anchors bead.
Both have the same shape and now the same fix: the package computes quantities that have
names and published sampling theory in this literature, and cites none of it. A reader who
knows Diedrichsen would recognise both the estimand and the variance problem immediately.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION, replacing everything I proposed earlier on this bead:
  1. cite Diedrichsen, Provost & Zareamoghaddam (2016) wherever the package discusses
     partition pairing or crossvalidated distances
  2. state that a spread across partition-pairs is not a valid standard error, that the
     understatement grows with effect size and with the number of partitions, and that
     leave-one-partition-out is the cheap correct alternative
  3. treat implementing the analytic covariance as a scope decision for the owner, not a
     defect - README:139's choice to export no uncertainty remains defensible

PROCESS NOTE ON MYSELF. I escalated this to claude-review twice, the second time to correct
the first. Both escalations were premature: one web search settled a question I twice told
the board I could not settle from inside the repository. I should have searched before
escalating, not after. That is the third instance in this workstream of the same error -
asserting from local reasoning where measurement or a lookup was available.
